entities.summary: Cynan ab Iago was a Welsh prince and leader of the House of Aberffraw, who played a crucial role in the medieval politics of Gwynedd and Wales. His family's history is deeply intertwined with the kingdom's, and his own legacy is marked by his contributions to the struggle for independence against English rule. Born into a world of tribal rivalries and shifting allegiances, Cynan ab Iago's life was shaped by the tumultuous landscape of 11th-century Wales. As a key figure in the Aberffraw dynasty, he navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Welsh kingdoms, seeking to strengthen his family's position and secure their future. His son, Gruffudd, would go on to play a significant role in the later history of Wales, becoming king in his own right and cementing the Aberffraw dynasty's place in Welsh history. Cynan ab Iago's story is one of power, family, and the enduring struggle for independence in the face of imperial expansion.
